description: The bar chart illustrates the average change in INC score when transitioning from the combined layer to the base layer across five different observation probability thresholds (0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9), with negative values indicating the base layer outperformed the combined layer and positive values indicating the reverse. The vertical axis, labeled “Average Change Using Compression,” ranges from -3 to +2, with tick marks at integer intervals. Each observation probability has two adjacent bars: gray bars represent input from “Inferred Frames,” and orange bars represent input from “Lexical Signal.” At observation probability 0.2, the gray bar is at approximately -2.8 and the orange bar is near 0.05; at 0.4, gray is at -2.7 and orange at 0.8; at 0.5, gray is at -2.3 and orange at 1.9; at 0.7, gray is at -1.6 and orange at 1.3; and at 0.9, gray is at -1.2 and orange at 1.5. Across all observation probabilities, the gray bars (inferred frames) consistently show negative values, indicating the base layer performed better, while the orange bars (lexical signal) are consistently positive, indicating the combined layer performed better — supporting the caption’s claim that inferred frames benefit the base layer and lexical signal improves the combined layer’s performance. The bars are grouped by observation probability along the horizontal axis, with no sorting by magnitude, and the legend at the bottom clarifies the color coding.
